speakers: Robert E. Murray (Graham Capital Management, COO)
summary: Marketing presentation asking why investors should hold systematic global macro (CTAs). Uses BSTI vs CSFB/Tremont hedge fund indices 1994-2008: correlations, stress months, skew/kurtosis, autocorrelation-adjusted IR and optimised portfolios. Concludes CTAs are uncorrelated, positively skewed crisis diversifiers deserving maximum allocation.

claims.speaker: Robert E. Murray
claims.quote: Positive autocorrelation of monthly returns leads to an increased volatility of annual returns.
claims.claim: Positive monthly autocorrelation makes annual volatility larger than sqrt(12) x monthly vol, so ignoring it understates risk.
claims.exact_rule: Var(annual) = 12*var_m*(1 + 2*sum_k (1-k/12)*rho_k); positive rho -> higher annual vol

claims.claim: Negative monthly autocorrelation makes annual volatility smaller than the sqrt(12) scaling implies.

reasoning.question: Why should a hedge fund or traditional portfolio allocate to systematic global macro (CTAs), and do standard statistics capture their benefit?

thesis.statement: CTAs (BSTI) have low or negative correlation to equities and hedge fund styles, positive returns in crisis months, positive skew and no return smoothing; once autocorrelation is accounted for, their risk-adjusted return is better and other styles worse, so optimised hedge fund portfolios should hold CTAs at the maximum weight.

foundations.premise: Smoothed (autocorrelated) monthly returns understate true volatility; correcting for it is needed for fair comparison.
Investors value diversification most in down markets, so conditional (down-month) correlation and stress returns matter.
Negative skew and fat tails are undesirable risks hidden by mean-variance statistics.
BSTI is a fair proxy for systematic global macro.

reasoning.forward_looking_inputs: (reader) No forecasting signal. The deck implies conditioning allocation on equity drawdowns is unnecessary because CTAs are naturally convex; for evaluating a macro book, measure down-month correlation, skew and autocorrelation-adjusted IR. The diversification would weaken in sharp V-shaped reversals or if CTA crowding raised correlation with equities.
reader_inferences: (reader) The CTA crisis returns come from trend following (short equities / long bonds in prolonged bear markets), not stated in the deck.
(reader) Weight bounds of 4%-20% are inferred from the weight table.
(reader) The EMN Nov 2008 -40% is a single-index event that drives its -12 skew.
(reader) Up/down months are presumably defined by the sign of the S&P 500 monthly return.
